newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu ousts Zaire prime minister, appoints general.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu ousts Zaire prime minister, appoints general.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko named a senior general as prime minister on Wednesday, replacing his veteran foe Etienne Tshisekedi less than a week after he took over the job, state television reported.

Mobutu, his hold over the sprawling Central African nation weakened by Laurent Kabila's rebels, appointed General Likulia Bolongo to replace Tshisekedi. Likulia was defence minister in the pre-Tshisekedi administration of Kengo wa Dondo.
"We won't take this lying down. They will find us in their path," one Tshisekedi aide told Reuters on hearing the news.

Earlier on Wednesday, security forces in Kinshasa fired in the air and used teargas against thousands of Tshisekedi supporters who turned out to accompany the radical leader to the prime minister's offices to install his new government team.
Security forces had blocked off the office complex with troops and armoured vehicles.

Tshisekedi, his eyes streaming from the teargas, had set off on foot for the offices surrounded by his supporters. Security forces fired in the air and fired teargas grenades after the crowd burst through an initial security cordon.

Witnesses said that Mobutu's son Kongolo, a presidential guard officer known in Kinshasa as "Saddam Hussein" after the Iraqi leader, had escorted Tshisekedi back home. Tshisekedi was bleeding from a wound to the head, one aide said.
The transitional parliament voted out Kengo following persistent charges that he mismanaged the war in the east.
The television said that Mobutu named a new prime minister because Zaire's political family had withdrawn its support for Tshisekedi.

Tshisekedi fell foul of Mobutu supporters and allies alike after announcing a government composed only of his most loyal followers. He earmaked six posts for rebels, who took up arms in October vowing to topple Mobutu, but the offer was rebuffed.
The rebels now control almost half of Zaire.
